headline: Kabinett clears Linnemann’s Pflege “kleine Lösung” (childless surcharge → 0.9% from Jan 2027); Chrome 154.0.8037.92 patches 32 bugs incl. Critical ANGLE CVE; EU draft offers conditional single-market access to candidates.

stories.title: Kabinett clears Pflege “kleine Lösung” — childless surcharge to 0.9%
facts: SPIEGEL/SZ (Wed): Federal Cabinet approved Health Minister Carsten Linnemann’s (CDU) care-insurance draft after overnight Union–SPD talks — morning brief still had Kabinett unresolved.
BMG via SZ/dpa: general Pflege contribution stays 3.6%; childless surcharge rises +0.3pp to 0.9% from 1 Jan 2027.
SPIEGEL: framed as a “kleine Lösung” to stabilize finances amid a multi-billion shortfall risk; SPD had threatened to block a pure cuts package.
Next week: formal decision for a Pflegekommission tasked with structural reforms, including models for balancing social and private care insurance (SPD priority).
Bill still needs Bundestag passage; exact cut details (e.g. care-grade rules, co-insured spouses) not fully public in today’s coverage.
stories.whyItMatters: Morning’s open coalition fight is over for now — a short-term contribution fix is in Cabinet, with the harder structural fight parked in a commission.

stories.title: Chrome 154.0.8037.92: 32 fixes, Critical ANGLE buffer overflow
facts: Chrome Releases (Tue): Stable → 154.0.8037.92/.93 (Win/Mac) and 154.0.8037.92 (Linux); rollout over coming days/weeks.
32 security fixes; top issue Critical CVE-2026-102331 — buffer overflow in ANGLE (reported by @mfx, 2026-08-24).
Batch is heavy on High memory-safety bugs (V8 type confusion, GPU/WebGPU uninitialized resources, use-after-free in Views/Passwords/PiP); Google has not reported exploitation in the wild.
Golem (Wed ~12:00 Berlin) amplified the Critical ANGLE hole for DE readers — update promptly.
stories.whyItMatters: Another large mid-cycle Chrome security drop weeks after 154’s launch — Critical graphics-stack memory bugs are the ones to chase first.

stories.title: EU draft: conditional single-market access for candidate countries
facts: POLITICO (Wed ~10:39 CEST): draft Commission “pre-enlargement” review (Alexandre Adam) would offer gradual single-market integration — frictionless trade + research access — while accession talks continue.
Economic benefits tied to foreign-policy alignment and not sharing key tech with hostile states/rivals; sensitive sectors flagged: semiconductors, quantum, biotech, AI, space.
Ukraine, Moldova, Albania, Montenegro get accelerated “road maps”; access is reversible if conditions fail.
Package due to top officials ~Oct 6 after von der Leyen’s Western Balkans trip; leaders debate at Oct 15 Brussels summit — also more QMV via passerelle clauses.
stories.whyItMatters: Brussels is trying to buy time and leverage on a stalled enlargement track by trading market access for alignment — with an explicit tech-security choke.

stories.title: Microsoft: WSL Containers generally available
facts: Windows Developer Blog (Sep 29): WSL Containers GA — `wsl --update` / GitHub release unlocks `wslc.exe` (alias `container.exe`) to build/run Linux containers on Windows without a separate engine.
Native apps can drive containers via NuGet `Microsoft.WSL.Containers` (C#/C++/WinRT) — Microsoft pitches local AI workloads and cloud-native apps on the desktop.

GA adds restart/cp/events/health checks, network connect/disconnect, configurable storage; Intune can allow/deny containers + registry allow-lists; Defender for Endpoint extends into container activity.
Roadmap: compose support next; heise (Wed ~11:53) notes WSL 3.0.1 (Sep 29) as the ship vehicle.
stories.whyItMatters: Windows is productizing a first-party Linux container runtime with enterprise controls — a direct alternative path to Docker Desktop for many Windows-dev workflows.
